tagline.text: An eco-park near Baguio with a glass walkway over the pine forest

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Peday, Barangay Loacan, Itogon, Benguet

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800~2,000 (per person per day, including admission and a meal inside the park)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), then overland to Baguio

children.text: This roughly 10-hectare eco-park in Loacan, Itogon, Benguet opened in February 2025. It has the Alapaap glass-floor walkway that juts about 19.8 m over a pine forest, paved forest trails, an open-air amphitheater and cafés. It is about 35 minutes by car from Baguio, so it works well as a half-day outing.

Mt. Camisong Forest Park and Events is an ecotourism park in Sitio Peday, Barangay Loacan, Itogon, Benguet. It is run by Mt. Camisong Property Management Inc., held a soft opening on January 27, 2025, and opened to the public on February 1, 2025. The park covers about
10 hectares
inside the Lower Agno Watershed Forest Reserve. According to an announcement from the Itogon municipal government, about 90% of the forest is preserved and less than one hectare has been developed.
The best-known feature is the Alapaap glass-floor walkway, which projects about

out from the ridge. From about 65 feet (roughly 20 m) above the pine canopy you can look down on the forest and out to the mountain ridges. The park also has paved forest trails, Samyo, an elevated tree walk among the pines, Dagitab, an open-air amphitheater, and a café and food hall that use regional ingredients, so you can walk, eat and relax in one place.

The park is a commercial venture, but it was designed to reduce its environmental load. Walkways were routed around existing tree roots and buildings are painted dark colors to blend into the forest. It has 363 solar panels (201 kW in total), a sewage treatment plant and an organic waste composting system. For that reason single-use plastic water bottles are confiscated at the gate, and outside food, pets and drones are not allowed.
It takes about
35 minutes

by car from central Baguio, so it is easy to fit into an itinerary. It is more of an outing for views, atmosphere and dining than a hiking destination. If you want a real hike, plan a separate trip to somewhere like Mount Ulap nearby. Prices and hours in this guide come from 2025–2026 articles, so check the park's official announcements before you go. The areas inside the park have their own names. Dagitab is the open-air amphitheater, Silakbo is the restroom block with floating mirrors, Binhi is an exhibit space about sustainability, Kalupi is the gift shop, Dalisay is a wooden children's playground, and Luntian and Kanlungan are event spaces. Kanlungan Hall is an indoor event venue that holds 40–60 people. Entry is through electronic gates after a bag inspection, and payment by cash, card, GCash and QR transfer is reportedly accepted. No environmental permit, local environmental fee or mandatory guide is reportedly required, but guided trail tours must be booked in advance.
This glass-floor walkway extends about

out from the ridge. It is built from three bonded layers of glass, and staff control how many people can walk on it at once. Queues grow on weekends, so go early. The glass is described as bulletproof-grade, and several publications call walking above the pines the highlight of the park.
A raised wooden walkway that winds high among the pine trees. It gives the feeling of walking at mid-height in the forest and is a popular photo spot.
All paths are paved. The easy trail is about
, the intermediate trail about
and the full Kahilom loop about
4.5 km

. Sneakers are enough. There are stairs and rolling sections, so comfortable shoes are better from the intermediate trail onward. An electric shuttle also loops around the park for families who find walking hard.

An open-air stage set against the pine forest. Local musicians and artists perform and exhibit here, so check the events schedule before you visit. In late 2025 events included an outdoor wire sculpture exhibit and a bazaar of local artists.
An open-air café serving Filipino comfort food and snacks, with multi-level viewing decks attached. It uses many Cordillera ingredients and produce from Benguet farms.
An all-glass restaurant beneath the glass walkway. It is meant for special meals and needs a reservation, which is essential in peak season.
A food hall with several concessionaires, where you can eat at a fairly modest price. Families and groups can each pick what they like.

The park has solar power, composting, rainwater catchment, filtered water refill stations, a wooden children's playground and art installations under the trees. The Kalupi gift shop sells plant-themed goods.

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: Morning walk and the glass walkway

children.text: Arrive when the park opens. Weekday mornings help you avoid fog and crowds. At the entrance your bag is inspected and single-use bottles are checked.
Walk the easy trail (about
) or the intermediate trail (about
) at an unhurried pace and enjoy the pine forest air.
Head to the Alapaap glass walkway. On weekends you will have to queue, so earlier in the morning is better.
Explore the Samyo tree walk, the Dagitab amphitheater and the viewing decks, and take photos.
Have an early lunch at the Muni-Muni Food Hall or Marahuyo Café.
Browse the Kalupi gift shop, then return to Baguio.
Fog usually covers the ridge from late morning, so take your view photos in the morning if you can.
Set out from near Pacdal in Baguio on the free electric shuttle, or by taxi or private car. Confirm that the shuttle is running before you go.
See the Alapaap walkway first, then start with the easy trail.
Walk the whole Kahilom loop (about
4.5 km
, about
2 hours
). The last trail entry is at 4 p.m.
Have lunch at Alapaap Dining or Marahuyo Café.
Rest at Dagitab or an exhibit area and look at works by local artists.
Enjoy the evening atmosphere, with the reported discount for entry after 5 p.m., and have dinner.
If you are driving back, leave before the mountain road gets dark.
Long-distance buses to Baguio run daily from Manila (Cubao, Pasay and elsewhere) and usually take
5~6 hours
. It can take longer depending on traffic and the time of day.
Fares vary by bus company and seat class, so check the exact amount locally.
After arriving in Baguio, reach the park by one of the methods below.
As of a November 2025 article, an electric bus ran free from Pacdal Circle near the Pacdal Police Station to the park. It ran roughly every two hours between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.
Seats are first come, first served and fill early on weekends. Whether the shuttle runs in 2026 and beyond, and its timetable, is not confirmed, so check the park's official announcements.
You can take a jeepney toward Loacan from central Baguio, get off near the Loacan entrance and ride a tricycle up. The jeepney fare is reportedly about
Tricycles are said to be hard to find at the gate for the ride back, so leave yourself plenty of time.
It is about
35 minutes
by car from Session Road in Baguio. A round-trip taxi with waiting time is reportedly negotiated at around
, so agree on the price beforehand.
One article reports parking at
. Mobile signal on the mountain road is unreliable, so download an offline map.
Clear skies and cool weather can be expected during the dry season from November to April. From December to February the ridge is quite cold in the morning, so bring a jacket.
In the rainy season the access road is slippery, and in bad weather hours may be shortened or the park may close. Check the park's official social media notices the night before.
The park reportedly gets about 1,500 visitors a day, and up to 3,500 on peak dry-season days. Fog usually covers the ridge around 11 a.m., so use the morning for views.

items.label: Students and BLISTT residents
items.note: Valid ID required; residents of Baguio, La Trinidad, Itogon, Sablan, Tuba and Tublay

items.label: Children
items.note: Articles say either 6 and under or under 7, so check locally

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

There is no lodging inside the park, so most visitors stay in Baguio and come for the day. It is about 35 minutes from Baguio, so a hotel around Burnham Park or Session Road makes getting here easy. Plan it together with your
Baguio
itinerary.

You are expected to eat at the restaurants inside the park. Outside food and drinks are not allowed, so plan lunch in advance. The Muni-Muni Food Hall is the cheapest, Marahuyo Café serves home-style food and Alapaap Dining is the glass restaurant. Dishes made with Benguet ingredients are known here, such as Strawberry Cansi, a sour beef soup made with underripe strawberries. Menus and prices change often, so check on site.
For a picnic there is the pre-booked Samyo private picnic. Sets for 4–8 people are reported at about
for a street-food basket, about
for chicken and waffles and about
for surf and turf. One estimate puts a family of four at roughly
with admission and mid-range meals, so treat it only as a budget reference.
Arriving at the 7 a.m. opening on a weekday helps you avoid fog and crowds.
The morning ridge is chilly. Bring a warm jacket rather than a thin hoodie.
Single-use plastic water bottles are confiscated at the entrance, so bring an empty tumbler and fill it at the refill stations.
Outside food is not allowed, so include meals inside the park in your budget.
The glass walkway has long queues on weekends. Aim for early morning or a weekday.
Student and BLISTT resident discounts require ID.
There is reportedly a discount for entry after 5 p.m., but it may change, so confirm it.
If you are driving back, leave before it gets dark.
In heavy rain or bad weather operations may be adjusted, so check official announcements before you go.
Pets and drones are prohibited, and the parking area is reportedly included.
The last trail entry is reportedly at 4 p.m., so if you arrive late you may not be able to walk the full loop.
Mobile signal can be weak on the access road, so download an offline map.
Fees, the shuttle and the free-entry age for children are based on 2025–2026 articles, so check the latest announcements.
Travelers wanting a serious hike may find it tame because the paths are paved.
A popular hiking route also in Itogon that takes about
4~6 hours
. If this park feels too easy, it is a good step up to a real mountain hike.
A good stop on the way back to Baguio, reportedly about
30 minutes
from Itogon.
The central city with lodging and restaurants, about
35 minutes
by car from the park.
Baguio's signature city park, a good follow-on for the afternoon or the next day.
